# Material catalogue

*Generated by `ultrafast reference materials` from `src/UltrafastEngine.Core/Data/materials/`; do not edit. Change a number in its catalogue file, then run `/regen`.*

Every number the engine takes from its material library is listed here with its unit (in the key name), its **status**, its uncertainty and its source.
How the files work, how to override a value and how runs report the values they used: [Materials](materials.md#the-material-catalogue).

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified` | the number was read from the cited source and compared; the comparison is recorded (`check`) |
| `approximate` | a typical, rounded or fitted value, good to the stated uncertainty; not traced to one table |
| `unverified` | not checked against any source; quoted from memory or from an earlier version of the code |

A run that uses an `approximate` or `unverified` value says so in its notes and lists it under `unverifiedInputs` in `summary.json`.

**185 quantities in 54 entries: 43 verified, 70 approximate, 70 unverified.**

### CS2

Liquid carbon disulfide, 20 C. Aliases: `CARBONDISULFIDE`, `CARBON_DISULFIDE`.

liquid CS2 at 20 C; index fit valid 0.5-1.6 um; n2 = 3.0e-18 m^2/W total (ps pulses) of which 10 % electronic and 90 % orientational, h(t) = (exp(-t/1.6 ps) - exp(-t/0.2 ps)) / 1.4 ps; the split and the time constants are unverified typical values (spread of the literature: a factor 2-3): override n2 / ramanFraction / raman.

## Gain media

### Yb:YAG

Ytterbium-doped YAG (quasi-three-level). Aliases: `ybyag`.

Yb:YAG cross sections are an analytic room-temperature fit; the McCumber relation gives reabsorption at the lasing wavelength (~0.1e-20 cm^2 at 1030 nm). Cryogenic linewidths are not modelled (only the Boltzmann factor follows temperatureK).

### Ti:sapphire

Titanium-doped sapphire (four-level). Aliases: `tisa`, `tisapphire`, `ti:sa`, `ti:al2o3`.

Ti:sapphire is treated as a four-level system (no lasing-band absorption); the residual infrared absorption (figure of merit) is not included -- add it with absorptionProfile or a material attenuation.

### LBO

lithium triborate, biaxial; the Kato (1994) set reproduces the handbook XY-plane type-I SHG angles (phi = 11.6 deg at 1064 nm, 13.8 deg at 1030 nm, 31.7 deg at 800 nm), the Chen / Hanson-Dick fit on refractiveindex.info gives 11.8 / 14.6 / 34.3 deg. Aliases: `lib3o5`.

LBO indices are room-temperature (no thermal model): non-critical phase matching by temperature is not modelled.
